rules: When assessing image quality, do not reward high contrast or stylized grain if it obscures fine details or introduces artifacts; instead, prioritize preservation of texture and edge clarity.
Do not assign high scores to images with dramatic color grading or saturation unless they enhance realism or emotional impact without distorting natural tones.
When content is culturally or historically significant (e.g., ancient carvings, architecture), prioritize legibility and structural integrity over artistic interpretation.

When assessing images with high-contrast lighting or strong artificial illumination, do not equate vividness or sharpness with higher quality; instead, evaluate whether the lighting enhances or detracts from perceived realism.
When judging images with low-light or night scenes, do not reward glow or luminance alone; instead, assess whether the scene appears natural or unnaturally enhanced.
When scoring any image, do not rely on isolated dimension scores without considering overall impression; instead, integrate technical, aesthetic, and content factors into a holistic judgment.
When assessing sharpness or detail, do not reward excessive noise or unnatural texture enhancement if it compromises the subject’s appearance or realism.
When evaluating color and lighting, prioritize visual harmony and emotional impact over mere vibrancy or contrast.
If the subject is obscured or distorted by foreground elements or shallow depth-of-field, score lower for content clarity even if technical metrics are high.
